answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may post offers or claim rewards. A harbor contract records the stake and assigns each account a unique cipher-linked registration; repeated identities do not multiply voting weight because weight is capped by stake and reputation earned through completed trades. The wharf is that honest newcomers face a real entry cost too, but an attacker must lock substantial capital across many accounts, risk slashing for proven fraud, and keep funds tied up while building history.
